newFindings.title: MC-04-ACCESSIBILITY-EVIDENCE.md disposition-count arithmetic is wrong
newFindings.evidence: Independent parse of the 28 QA rows (raw/claims-audit.json): PASS 4 (QA-16, 21, 25, 27), PARTIAL 16, NOT_TESTED 5, BLOCKED 3 = 28. The document states 'PASS 4 · PARTIAL 13 · NOT_TESTED 6 · BLOCKED 3 (28 total)': PARTIAL understated by 3, NOT_TESTED overstated by 1, and the stated parts sum to 26, not 28. Individual QA dispositions are correct and conservative; only the count line is wrong.
newFindings.impact: A reviewer or reader could take the counts at face value; the error is in the direction of looking less complete than the record actually is, but the line is contradictory (26 ≠ 28).
newFindings.disposition: OPEN — correct the count line to 4/16/5/3.

newFindings.title: TYPOGRAPHY-SYSTEM.md says only the numeric role moves family, but units and timestamps also move from DM Sans (brief §4.4) to Manrope
newFindings.evidence: §5 table: 'Unit / suffix | Manrope 500' and 'Timestamp / age | Manrope 500–600, tabular'; the brief's §4.4 table assigns Unit/suffix to DM Sans 500 and metadata/timestamps to DM Sans 400–500. The summary sentence claims 'The numeric role is the only role that moves family relative to the brief's §4.4 table'. The token JSON also lists 'units' under displayNumeric roles.
newFindings.impact: Documentation accuracy of a deviation record; the deviation itself is justified (units must not inherit proportional digits from a different family) but should be recorded as covering the whole numeric treatment bundle, not one row.
newFindings.disposition: OPEN — reword the deviation to 'numeric treatment (value + unit + timestamp/age spans)', or state explicitly that units and timestamps follow the numeric family.
